# @future-standard-ui

> React 19 component library from Future Standard, published as individually installable packages
> under the `@future-standard-ui` scope. Schema-driven, framework-agnostic cores with React
> renderers on top; CSS modules with a data-attribute contract; design tokens as CSS custom
> properties from `@future-standard-ui/theme`.

Conventions: pnpm monorepo (Turborepo), Biome for lint/format, Vitest for tests. Never `npx`.
Components are styled through `@layer component` and overridden in `@layer overrides` via the
un-hashed `data-ui="<part>"` attributes each component emits.

## Docs

- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): where everything lives and the conventions.
- [Building a Component playbook](docs/playbooks/building-a-component.md): the process every
  component follows, with a dated lessons log.
- [Meta-package strategy](docs/META_PACKAGES.md): how packages group.

## Table

- [Schema quickstart for agents](docs/components/table/schema-quickstart.md): produce a valid
  table schema quickly — rules, template, recipes, checklist.
- [Schema reference](docs/components/table/schema.md): every property, default and runtime option.
- [JSON Schema](packages/table-core/schema/table.schema.json): machine-readable definition
  (`@future-standard-ui/table-core/schema.json`).
- [Standard cells](docs/components/table/cells.md): cell types and their JSON options; the
  `onCellAction` channel.
- [Table guide](docs/components/table/README.md): install, usage, props, primitives, overrides,
  accessibility, migration from the old kit's `TypeTable`.
- [DOM contract](docs/components/table/dom-contract.md): parts and attributes; how to write a
  renderer for another framework.
- [Plan and decisions](docs/plans/table.md): why the table is built this way.

## Packages

- `@future-standard-ui/theme`: tokens (colours, fonts, spacing) as CSS custom properties, light/dark.
- `@future-standard-ui/button`, `icon-button`, `loading-button`.
- `@future-standard-ui/table-core` (no React), `table` (React), `table-cells`, `tables` (meta).
- `@future-standard-ui/ui-kit`: kitchen-sink re-export of everything.

## Examples

`pnpm build && pnpm dev` serves `apps/dev`; each example is a hash route
(`#/table-cameras`, `#/table-clips`, `#/table-responsive`, `#/table-cells`, `#/table-vanilla`,
`#/table-primitives`).
